Fix Xcode 16.1 build (#1430)

* Force @MainActor on MediaLoader completion closures

Swift 6.1 (Xcode 16.4) doesn't always infer that a trailing closure
passed to an `@escaping @MainActor (...) -> Void` parameter is itself
`@MainActor`-isolated, especially when the call site is nested inside
SwiftUI view-builder / `.onAppear` / `.task` closures. Swift 6.2
(Xcode 26.x) relaxed this via improved closure isolation inference, so
the same code compiles there but fails the Xcode 16.x builds
(`Build Demo App (16.4)` and `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)`).

Add explicit `@MainActor` to the trailing closures passed to the new
`MediaLoader` API, `MediaAttachment.generateThumbnail`, and
`MessageController.downloadAttachment` so isolation is unambiguous on
every supported Swift version.

* [CI] Disable xcbeautify/xcpretty in test_ui and build_demo lanes

The previous commit's @MainActor fix still leaves the Xcode 16.4
`Build Demo App (16.4)` and Xcode 16.1 `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)` jobs
red, and we can't see the actual Swift compiler diagnostic because
fastlane scan's formatter (xcbeautify / xcpretty) is swallowing the
`error:` lines emitted by xcodebuild.

Pass `output_style: 'raw'`, `disable_xcpretty: true`, and an empty
`xcodebuild_formatter` to both scan invocations so the raw xcodebuild
output — including the Swift error — makes it into the GH Actions log.

* Work around Swift 6.0 SILGen crash on Utils() default argument

Raw Xcode 16.1 logs show the Swift compiler crashes in SILGen while
synthesizing the default-argument thunk for `utils: Utils = Utils()` on
`StreamChat.init`. The stack trace bottoms out at `emitRawApply` from
`SILGen default arg initializer` at StreamChat.swift:18 (`"Utils("`),
an assertion that was silently fixed in Swift 6.2.

The crash is triggered by `Utils.init` now accepting `mediaLoader:
MediaLoader? = nil` — a protocol-existential parameter from an external
module — combined with `@MainActor` isolation on `Utils` and the fact
that the `Utils()` expression itself lives in another default-argument
slot of a different `@MainActor` initializer.

Move the `Utils()` construction out of the default-argument slot and
into the initializer body by switching `utils` to an optional with a
`nil` default. This is source-compatible: every existing caller of
`StreamChat(chatClient:)`, `StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:)`, and
`StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:utils:)` still type-checks without
changes (`Utils` coerces to `Utils?`).

Fix swipe-to-reply gesture conflicting with message list scrolling (#1431)

* Fix swipe-to-reply gesture blocking message list scrolling

The swipe-to-reply drag recognizer was attached with `.gesture()` and
only compared total translation magnitude against `minimumSwipeDistance`,
with no axis awareness. This caused it to sporadically win the gesture
competition against the enclosing `ScrollView`'s pan recognizer on
diagonal or slow vertical drags, freezing the list until the finger
lifted.

Switch to `.simultaneousGesture(DragGesture())` and gate `offsetX`
updates on a per-event horizontal-dominance check
(`abs(dx) > abs(dy) * 1.5`). The scroll view's pan recognizer always
runs alongside uncontested, and the bubble only moves when the motion
is clearly horizontal. Direction is re-evaluated on every event so no
persistent state can leak across gestures.

* Simplify fix

* Prevent swipe-to-reply from competing with list scrolling

Track the message list scroll phase on newer SwiftUI versions and disable the swipe-to-reply modifier while scrolling is active. This keeps vertical list scrolling in control once a real scroll begins, instead of letting row-level swipe gestures stay attached and interfere.

Fix timestamp animation glitch on swipe-to-reply (#1360)

* Fix timestamp snapping back faster than delivery indicator on swipe-to-reply

The deprecated `.animation(nil)` modifier on `MessageDateView` was
stripping the animation transaction for all property changes, causing
the timestamp to jump instantly while the rest of the message animated
with the swipe-to-reply spring curve. Scoping it to
`.animation(nil, value: text)` only suppresses animation on text
content changes while allowing positional animations to propagate.

Fix Xcode 16.1 build (#1430)

* Force @MainActor on MediaLoader completion closures

Swift 6.1 (Xcode 16.4) doesn't always infer that a trailing closure
passed to an `@escaping @MainActor (...) -> Void` parameter is itself
`@MainActor`-isolated, especially when the call site is nested inside
SwiftUI view-builder / `.onAppear` / `.task` closures. Swift 6.2
(Xcode 26.x) relaxed this via improved closure isolation inference, so
the same code compiles there but fails the Xcode 16.x builds
(`Build Demo App (16.4)` and `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)`).

Add explicit `@MainActor` to the trailing closures passed to the new
`MediaLoader` API, `MediaAttachment.generateThumbnail`, and
`MessageController.downloadAttachment` so isolation is unambiguous on
every supported Swift version.

* [CI] Disable xcbeautify/xcpretty in test_ui and build_demo lanes

The previous commit's @MainActor fix still leaves the Xcode 16.4
`Build Demo App (16.4)` and Xcode 16.1 `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)` jobs
red, and we can't see the actual Swift compiler diagnostic because
fastlane scan's formatter (xcbeautify / xcpretty) is swallowing the
`error:` lines emitted by xcodebuild.

Pass `output_style: 'raw'`, `disable_xcpretty: true`, and an empty
`xcodebuild_formatter` to both scan invocations so the raw xcodebuild
output — including the Swift error — makes it into the GH Actions log.

* Work around Swift 6.0 SILGen crash on Utils() default argument

Raw Xcode 16.1 logs show the Swift compiler crashes in SILGen while
synthesizing the default-argument thunk for `utils: Utils = Utils()` on
`StreamChat.init`. The stack trace bottoms out at `emitRawApply` from
`SILGen default arg initializer` at StreamChat.swift:18 (`"Utils("`),
an assertion that was silently fixed in Swift 6.2.

The crash is triggered by `Utils.init` now accepting `mediaLoader:
MediaLoader? = nil` — a protocol-existential parameter from an external
module — combined with `@MainActor` isolation on `Utils` and the fact
that the `Utils()` expression itself lives in another default-argument
slot of a different `@MainActor` initializer.

Move the `Utils()` construction out of the default-argument slot and
into the initializer body by switching `utils` to an optional with a
`nil` default. This is source-compatible: every existing caller of
`StreamChat(chatClient:)`, `StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:)`, and
`StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:utils:)` still type-checks without
changes (`Utils` coerces to `Utils?`).

Fix swipe-to-reply gesture conflicting with message list scrolling (#1431)

* Fix swipe-to-reply gesture blocking message list scrolling

The swipe-to-reply drag recognizer was attached with `.gesture()` and
only compared total translation magnitude against `minimumSwipeDistance`,
with no axis awareness. This caused it to sporadically win the gesture
competition against the enclosing `ScrollView`'s pan recognizer on
diagonal or slow vertical drags, freezing the list until the finger
lifted.

Switch to `.simultaneousGesture(DragGesture())` and gate `offsetX`
updates on a per-event horizontal-dominance check
(`abs(dx) > abs(dy) * 1.5`). The scroll view's pan recognizer always
runs alongside uncontested, and the bubble only moves when the motion
is clearly horizontal. Direction is re-evaluated on every event so no
persistent state can leak across gestures.

* Simplify fix

* Prevent swipe-to-reply from competing with list scrolling

Track the message list scroll phase on newer SwiftUI versions and disable the swipe-to-reply modifier while scrolling is active. This keeps vertical list scrolling in control once a real scroll begins, instead of letting row-level swipe gestures stay attached and interfere.

* Fix edit confirmation briefly flashing send button before microphone

Align the edited/quoted message binding resets with `clearText()`'s
deferred `text = ""` update. When an optimistic edit API completion
fires before the ~0.1s delayed text clear, the trailing composer
button would transition ConfirmEdit → Send → Mic instead of
ConfirmEdit → Mic. Deferring both binding resets by the same delay
keeps `MessageComposerInputState` out of `.creating(hasContent: true)`
during the gap, so the button switches directly to the microphone.

* Fix shared AVPlayer breaking when sending while voice preview plays

Release the shared audio player's reference to the composer's local
voice recording file before the flow can move it into upload. Previously
`confirmRecording`, `discardRecording`, and `sendMessage` left the
singleton AVPlayer playing the local temp URL. On successful upload,
`AttachmentQueueUploader` removes that file, leaving the AVPlayer's
currentItem pointed at a dangling asset and breaking playback for every
voice message in the message list until the player is re-created.

`stopPreviewPlaybackIfNeeded()` only stops the player when the composer
actually has local voice recordings pending/added, so unrelated
message-list playback isn't disrupted on text-only sends.

Add an opt-out `showsPressedState` flag to `StreamIconButton` /
`StreamButtonStyle` and use it from `PlayPauseButton` so toggling
play/pause no longer fades the pressed-state gray overlay in and out.
Also switch the inline play/pause button in the recording preview to
`.buttonStyle(.plain)` to suppress the default label dim on press.

When the reactions overlay displays a message preview
(`shownAsPreview == true`), the existing tap-swallowing gesture on the
bubble only blocked SwiftUI taps, so UIKit-backed controls like the
voice recording waveform slider were still interactive while the user
inspected the preview. Disabling hit testing on the inner `MessageView`
inside the preview stops all attachments — voice recordings, galleries,
polls — from being interactable in the overlay, matching the
already-expected behavior for images.

Fix image attachment flicker on reaction and Giphy not refreshing on shuffle (#1439)

* Fix image attachment loading flicker when reacting to messages

`StreamAsyncImage` previously dropped back to the `.loading` phase
whenever the URL changed — including the trivial change reactions cause
when SwiftUI re-asks for the same attachment with a freshly signed
CDN URL — which produced a brief loading indicator over an
already-cached image.

The view now keeps the previously loaded image on screen until the
loader returns the new one, and only ever surfaces `.loading` when no
image has been rendered yet. The whole `NukeImageLoader` synchronous
cache lookup machinery is gone; `StreamAsyncImage` relies on the
configured `MediaLoader` for caching, which is what every other
loading entry point in the SDK already does.

Resize dimensions are still rounded to integer points so sub-point
layout jitter (for example 251.999 vs 252.0) keeps mapping to the same
CDN URL and the same cache entry.

* Allow seeding StreamAsyncImage with a pre-loaded UIImage

Adds an `image:` parameter to the URL initializer and a UIImage-only
initializer so callers that already have the bitmap in memory can hand
it to `StreamAsyncImage` directly. The seeded image is stored as the
initial `@State` phase, so the very first render shows it — no
placeholder, no loading spinner — and any URL-driven load runs in the
background and replaces the seed once it resolves.

A failed reload no longer wipes a previously rendered image either:
once the view has shown a successful result it stays on screen until a
new successful load arrives, or the view is torn down.

Useful for entry points like the reactions overlay where the message
re-mounts in a fresh view tree and would otherwise start at the empty
phase even when the image is still in the cache.

`StreamCDNRequester.buildCachingKey` at the LLC layer; the SwiftUI
view only needs a stable identifier per `(image path, render size)`
pair so the task doesn't churn.

Fix attachment and quoted-message taps not working on iOS 17 (#1443)

* Fix attachment and quoted-message taps not working on iOS 17

`MessageContainerView` attached a `.highPriorityGesture(TapGesture(),
including: shownAsPreview ? .all : .none)` to the message bubble so
that taps would be swallowed while the bubble is rendered inside the
reactions overlay. On iOS 17 SwiftUI still arbitrates touches through
the recognizer even when `including: .none` is set, which starved
descendant tap recognizers (image attachments, quoted messages, link
previews, …) of touches and made them feel completely unresponsive.

The swallow gesture is no longer required at all: the reactions
overlay already prevents the inner content from reacting to taps via
`.allowsHitTesting(!shownAsPreview)`, so removing the modifier across
all iOS versions fixes the iOS 17 regression without any visible
behavior change on iOS 18+.

stripping the animation transaction for all property changes, causing
the timestamp to jump instantly while the rest of the message animated
with the swipe-to-reply spring curve. Scoping it to

content changes while allowing positional animations to propagate.

Fix Xcode 16.1 build (#1430)

* Force @MainActor on MediaLoader completion closures

Swift 6.1 (Xcode 16.4) doesn't always infer that a trailing closure
passed to an `@escaping @MainActor (...) -> Void` parameter is itself
`@MainActor`-isolated, especially when the call site is nested inside
SwiftUI view-builder / `.onAppear` / `.task` closures. Swift 6.2
(Xcode 26.x) relaxed this via improved closure isolation inference, so
the same code compiles there but fails the Xcode 16.x builds
(`Build Demo App (16.4)` and `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)`).

Add explicit `@MainActor` to the trailing closures passed to the new
`MediaLoader` API, `MediaAttachment.generateThumbnail`, and
`MessageController.downloadAttachment` so isolation is unambiguous on
every supported Swift version.

* [CI] Disable xcbeautify/xcpretty in test_ui and build_demo lanes

The previous commit's @MainActor fix still leaves the Xcode 16.4
`Build Demo App (16.4)` and Xcode 16.1 `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)` jobs
red, and we can't see the actual Swift compiler diagnostic because
fastlane scan's formatter (xcbeautify / xcpretty) is swallowing the
`error:` lines emitted by xcodebuild.

Pass `output_style: 'raw'`, `disable_xcpretty: true`, and an empty
`xcodebuild_formatter` to both scan invocations so the raw xcodebuild
output — including the Swift error — makes it into the GH Actions log.

* Work around Swift 6.0 SILGen crash on Utils() default argument

Raw Xcode 16.1 logs show the Swift compiler crashes in SILGen while
synthesizing the default-argument thunk for `utils: Utils = Utils()` on
`StreamChat.init`. The stack trace bottoms out at `emitRawApply` from
`SILGen default arg initializer` at StreamChat.swift:18 (`"Utils("`),
an assertion that was silently fixed in Swift 6.2.

The crash is triggered by `Utils.init` now accepting `mediaLoader:
MediaLoader? = nil` — a protocol-existential parameter from an external
module — combined with `@MainActor` isolation on `Utils` and the fact
that the `Utils()` expression itself lives in another default-argument
slot of a different `@MainActor` initializer.

Move the `Utils()` construction out of the default-argument slot and
into the initializer body by switching `utils` to an optional with a
`nil` default. This is source-compatible: every existing caller of
`StreamChat(chatClient:)`, `StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:)`, and
`StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:utils:)` still type-checks without
changes (`Utils` coerces to `Utils?`).

Fix swipe-to-reply gesture conflicting with message list scrolling (#1431)

* Fix swipe-to-reply gesture blocking message list scrolling

The swipe-to-reply drag recognizer was attached with `.gesture()` and
only compared total translation magnitude against `minimumSwipeDistance`,
with no axis awareness. This caused it to sporadically win the gesture
competition against the enclosing `ScrollView`'s pan recognizer on
diagonal or slow vertical drags, freezing the list until the finger
lifted.

Switch to `.simultaneousGesture(DragGesture())` and gate `offsetX`
updates on a per-event horizontal-dominance check
(`abs(dx) > abs(dy) * 1.5`). The scroll view's pan recognizer always
runs alongside uncontested, and the bubble only moves when the motion
is clearly horizontal. Direction is re-evaluated on every event so no
persistent state can leak across gestures.

* Prevent swipe-to-reply from competing with list scrolling

Track the message list scroll phase on newer SwiftUI versions and disable the swipe-to-reply modifier while scrolling is active. This keeps vertical list scrolling in control once a real scroll begins, instead of letting row-level swipe gestures stay attached and interfere.

Fix image attachment flicker on reaction and Giphy not refreshing on shuffle (#1439)

* Fix image attachment loading flicker when reacting to messages

`StreamAsyncImage` previously dropped back to the `.loading` phase
whenever the URL changed — including the trivial change reactions cause
when SwiftUI re-asks for the same attachment with a freshly signed
CDN URL — which produced a brief loading indicator over an
already-cached image.

The view now keeps the previously loaded image on screen until the
loader returns the new one, and only ever surfaces `.loading` when no
image has been rendered yet. The whole `NukeImageLoader` synchronous
cache lookup machinery is gone; `StreamAsyncImage` relies on the
configured `MediaLoader` for caching, which is what every other
loading entry point in the SDK already does.

Resize dimensions are still rounded to integer points so sub-point
layout jitter (for example 251.999 vs 252.0) keeps mapping to the same
CDN URL and the same cache entry.

* Allow seeding StreamAsyncImage with a pre-loaded UIImage

Adds an `image:` parameter to the URL initializer and a UIImage-only
initializer so callers that already have the bitmap in memory can hand
it to `StreamAsyncImage` directly. The seeded image is stored as the
initial `@State` phase, so the very first render shows it — no
placeholder, no loading spinner — and any URL-driven load runs in the
background and replaces the seed once it resolves.

A failed reload no longer wipes a previously rendered image either:
once the view has shown a successful result it stays on screen until a
new successful load arrives, or the view is torn down.

Useful for entry points like the reactions overlay where the message
re-mounts in a fresh view tree and would otherwise start at the empty
phase even when the image is still in the cache.

Fix attachment and quoted-message taps not working on iOS 17 (#1443)

* Fix attachment and quoted-message taps not working on iOS 17

`MessageContainerView` attached a `.highPriorityGesture(TapGesture(),
including: shownAsPreview ? .all : .none)` to the message bubble so
that taps would be swallowed while the bubble is rendered inside the
reactions overlay. On iOS 17 SwiftUI still arbitrates touches through
the recognizer even when `including: .none` is set, which starved
descendant tap recognizers (image attachments, quoted messages, link
previews, …) of touches and made them feel completely unresponsive.

The swallow gesture is no longer required at all: the reactions
overlay already prevents the inner content from reacting to taps via
`.allowsHitTesting(!shownAsPreview)`, so removing the modifier across
all iOS versions fixes the iOS 17 regression without any visible
behavior change on iOS 18+.

  so VoiceOver users can reorder via the rotor without a drag gesture.
- Label the Max Votes stepper buttons "Decrease vote limit" / "Increase
  vote limit", apply `.disabled(!enabled)` so the disabled trait is exposed
  at the bounds, and expose the current value through a "Vote limit, N"
  static text element. This replaces the misleading "Remove, button"
  inferred from the SF Symbol.
- Combine the title + description + switch rows in `CreatePollSettingCard`
  and the multiple-votes / vote-limit toggle rows into single accessibility
  elements via `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`, so each is read
  as one element ("{title}, {description}, switch, {state}") instead of
  splitting focus across the text and toggle.

Adds unit tests for the new `moveOption(id:direction:)` and
`reorderableOptionCount` view-model helpers, and updates the localization
strings under `composer.polls.accessibility.*`.

Improve Create Poll view UX (#1464)

* Improve keyboard UX in CreatePollView

Wire up SwiftUI's Focus API so the keyboard's Next return key advances
between the question and option text fields, and dismiss the keyboard
interactively while scrolling the list. Focus is gated on iOS 15+ and
scroll-to-dismiss on iOS 16+; older OS versions keep the existing
behavior. Pure SwiftUI, no UIKit bridging.

* Reduce duplication in CreatePollView fields

Hide the iOS 15 availability split behind a `createPollFields` helper so
the parent body has a single entry point, and extract a
`CreatePollFieldFocus` view modifier so the focus chain
(`.focused`/`.submitLabel`/`.onSubmit`) is applied uniformly without
repeating it on each text field.

The question container and option row now own their `TextField` and
expose a `decorate` closure, removing the duplicate text-field
construction between the iOS 14 fallback and the iOS 15+ focused path.

The two helpers are `@ViewBuilder` functions rather than wrapper views
so the resulting `_ConditionalContent` and `ForEach` land directly in
the enclosing `List`'s `TupleView` and are still expanded into one row
per field.

* Extract CreatePollView input fields into dedicated views

Replaces the createPollFields and createPollOptionRows @ViewBuilder
functions with CreatePollInputFields and CreatePollOptionRows view
structs so SwiftUI can diff and skip re-evaluation when inputs are
unchanged. Renames CreatePollFocusField to CreatePollInputField and
CreatePollFieldFocus to CreatePollInputFieldFocus to make the input
field intent explicit at call sites.

* Split CreatePollView form into Question and Options views

Replaces CreatePollInputFields (and its variants) with CreatePollForm,
a thin focus coordinator that composes two prominent section views:
CreatePollQuestion (the question label + text field) and
CreatePollOptions (the options label + reorderable rows). Each section
exposes a decorator closure so the focused-form variant can layer
keyboard navigation modifiers without duplicating chrome.

* Extract CreatePollMultipleVotesCard into its own view

Moves the inline multipleVotesCard computed property out of
CreatePollView and into a dedicated CreatePollMultipleVotesCard
struct alongside CreatePollSettingCard, so CreatePollView's body
stays focused on layout.

Fix Xcode 16.1 build (#1430)

* Force @MainActor on MediaLoader completion closures

Swift 6.1 (Xcode 16.4) doesn't always infer that a trailing closure
passed to an `@escaping @MainActor (...) -> Void` parameter is itself
`@MainActor`-isolated, especially when the call site is nested inside
SwiftUI view-builder / `.onAppear` / `.task` closures. Swift 6.2
(Xcode 26.x) relaxed this via improved closure isolation inference, so
the same code compiles there but fails the Xcode 16.x builds
(`Build Demo App (16.4)` and `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)`).

Add explicit `@MainActor` to the trailing closures passed to the new
`MediaLoader` API, `MediaAttachment.generateThumbnail`, and
`MessageController.downloadAttachment` so isolation is unambiguous on
every supported Swift version.

* [CI] Disable xcbeautify/xcpretty in test_ui and build_demo lanes

The previous commit's @MainActor fix still leaves the Xcode 16.4
`Build Demo App (16.4)` and Xcode 16.1 `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)` jobs
red, and we can't see the actual Swift compiler diagnostic because
fastlane scan's formatter (xcbeautify / xcpretty) is swallowing the
`error:` lines emitted by xcodebuild.

Pass `output_style: 'raw'`, `disable_xcpretty: true`, and an empty
`xcodebuild_formatter` to both scan invocations so the raw xcodebuild
output — including the Swift error — makes it into the GH Actions log.

* Work around Swift 6.0 SILGen crash on Utils() default argument

Raw Xcode 16.1 logs show the Swift compiler crashes in SILGen while
synthesizing the default-argument thunk for `utils: Utils = Utils()` on
`StreamChat.init`. The stack trace bottoms out at `emitRawApply` from
`SILGen default arg initializer` at StreamChat.swift:18 (`"Utils("`),
an assertion that was silently fixed in Swift 6.2.

The crash is triggered by `Utils.init` now accepting `mediaLoader:
MediaLoader? = nil` — a protocol-existential parameter from an external
module — combined with `@MainActor` isolation on `Utils` and the fact
that the `Utils()` expression itself lives in another default-argument
slot of a different `@MainActor` initializer.

Move the `Utils()` construction out of the default-argument slot and
into the initializer body by switching `utils` to an optional with a
`nil` default. This is source-compatible: every existing caller of
`StreamChat(chatClient:)`, `StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:)`, and
`StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:utils:)` still type-checks without
changes (`Utils` coerces to `Utils?`).

Fix swipe-to-reply gesture conflicting with message list scrolling (#1431)

* Fix swipe-to-reply gesture blocking message list scrolling

The swipe-to-reply drag recognizer was attached with `.gesture()` and
only compared total translation magnitude against `minimumSwipeDistance`,
with no axis awareness. This caused it to sporadically win the gesture
competition against the enclosing `ScrollView`'s pan recognizer on
diagonal or slow vertical drags, freezing the list until the finger
lifted.

Switch to `.simultaneousGesture(DragGesture())` and gate `offsetX`
updates on a per-event horizontal-dominance check
(`abs(dx) > abs(dy) * 1.5`). The scroll view's pan recognizer always
runs alongside uncontested, and the bubble only moves when the motion
is clearly horizontal. Direction is re-evaluated on every event so no
persistent state can leak across gestures.

* Prevent swipe-to-reply from competing with list scrolling

Track the message list scroll phase on newer SwiftUI versions and disable the swipe-to-reply modifier while scrolling is active. This keeps vertical list scrolling in control once a real scroll begins, instead of letting row-level swipe gestures stay attached and interfere.

Fix image attachment flicker on reaction and Giphy not refreshing on shuffle (#1439)

* Fix image attachment loading flicker when reacting to messages

`StreamAsyncImage` previously dropped back to the `.loading` phase
whenever the URL changed — including the trivial change reactions cause
when SwiftUI re-asks for the same attachment with a freshly signed
CDN URL — which produced a brief loading indicator over an
already-cached image.

The view now keeps the previously loaded image on screen until the
loader returns the new one, and only ever surfaces `.loading` when no
image has been rendered yet. The whole `NukeImageLoader` synchronous
cache lookup machinery is gone; `StreamAsyncImage` relies on the
configured `MediaLoader` for caching, which is what every other
loading entry point in the SDK already does.

Resize dimensions are still rounded to integer points so sub-point
layout jitter (for example 251.999 vs 252.0) keeps mapping to the same
CDN URL and the same cache entry.

* Allow seeding StreamAsyncImage with a pre-loaded UIImage

Adds an `image:` parameter to the URL initializer and a UIImage-only
initializer so callers that already have the bitmap in memory can hand
it to `StreamAsyncImage` directly. The seeded image is stored as the
initial `@State` phase, so the very first render shows it — no
placeholder, no loading spinner — and any URL-driven load runs in the
background and replaces the seed once it resolves.

A failed reload no longer wipes a previously rendered image either:
once the view has shown a successful result it stays on screen until a
new successful load arrives, or the view is torn down.

Useful for entry points like the reactions overlay where the message
re-mounts in a fresh view tree and would otherwise start at the empty

Improve composer RTL support (#1478)

* Fix composer input alignment so spaces render in RTL (IOS-1666)

Forcing `.right`/`.left` text alignment on the composer's UITextView caused
trailing whitespace to be visually trimmed, which made pressing the
spacebar appear to do nothing in an RTL composer. Use `.natural` for the
text view itself so bidi resolves trailing characters correctly, and keep
the explicit alignment on the placeholder label so it still appears on the
expected side of an empty composer.

* Support RTL voice recording gestures and slide-to-cancel (IOS-1668)

The voice recording flow was designed assuming the mic button lives on
the trailing/right edge of the composer and that the user cancels by
swiping left. In RTL the mic sits on the left, so the user naturally
swipes right to cancel, which made the gesture, the slide-to-cancel
label offset, and the cancel threshold all read the wrong values.

Normalize the drag translation in the gesture overlay so downstream
cancel logic always treats negative X as "toward cancel" regardless of
layout direction, and mirror the slide-to-cancel label's visible offset
back into screen coordinates so it follows the finger in both LTR and
RTL.

* Stop attachments tray from shifting on insert in RTL (IOS-1669)

The attachments tray was applying `.animation(.default)` to the whole
container, which animates every implicit layout change as items are
added or removed. In RTL the HStack grows toward the visual leading
edge, so existing attachments appeared to slide whenever a new one
was inserted. Scope the animation to the empty/non-empty transition
so the scale transition still plays once, while individual insertions
no longer drag the rest of the tray around.

Also flip the horizontal offset on the dismiss button overlay so the
close button pokes out of the correct corner in RTL instead of being
nudged back inside the attachment.

* Slide RTL voice cancel label toward duration, not mic (IOS-1668)

`SlideToCancelLabel.slideOffset` was mirroring the X value for RTL, but
SwiftUI's `.offset(x:)` already mirrors its horizontal value in an RTL
layout. Combined, the label slid leftward toward the mic when the user
dragged to cancel in RTL instead of rightward toward the duration.

Drop the explicit RTL mirror on the label offset. The gesture overlay
still normalizes the drag translation so cancel-threshold checks keep
working in both layout directions.

* Anchor RTL attachments tray so existing items stay put (IOS-1669)

Scoping the implicit `.animation(.default)` to `composerAssets.isEmpty`
in the previous attempt only suppressed the entrance/exit animation
from replaying on every insert. The visible shift remained because the
horizontal ScrollView anchors its content to absolute x=0 while an RTL
HStack grows toward the visible leading edge — so appending a new asset
keeps inserting it at x=0 and pushes every already-visible thumbnail to
the right.

Render the assets in reverse order in RTL so newly appended items land
at the off-screen trailing side of the HStack, leaving the existing
thumbnails fixed in place when a new one is added.

* Prepend new RTL attachments instead of reversing the displayed list

Move the RTL fix from a reversed copy computed on every render to a
local @State array that mirrors `assets` in LTR and prepends newly
added entries at index 0 in RTL. The shift was caused by where the
new asset is inserted into the HStack, so the change now happens at
insertion time rather than reordering the entire list on each layout
pass.

* Scroll to the newest attachment after insertion in RTL composer

In LTR the tray scrolls to a tail anchor at the end of the HStack to
reveal the just-inserted asset. In RTL the new asset is prepended and
sits at the visual leading edge (right), so the tail anchor scrolls
the wrong way and the new attachment stays hidden. Scroll to the new
asset's id with the leading anchor in RTL so it's brought back into
view, matching the LTR behavior.

* Let the HStack lay out RTL attachments naturally and scroll to the new one

The previous attempts (reverse the displayed array, then maintain a
local @State and prepend new entries) put the just-added asset at the
visual right in RTL, which doesn't match how the rest of the SDK lays
out trailing content. Drop the custom ordering and rely on HStack's
native RTL behavior so new attachments land at the visual left, then
pick the scroll anchor that matches the current direction (.trailing
in LTR, .leading in RTL) so `scrollTo(tailId, anchor:)` reveals the
new asset on whichever edge it actually landed.

* Snap composer attachment thumbnails on insert and remove

The default layout-shift animation on the HStack made the remaining
thumbnails appear to slide sideways every time an asset was added or
removed. Drop the animation inside the HStack with a transaction so
the thumbnails snap to their new positions. The scroll-to-new-asset
animation lives on the parent ScrollView so it keeps its smooth
behavior.

* Scroll to the new attachment in one smooth movement

The 250ms delay before scrolling existed so the previous layout
animation could settle. Now that the thumbnails snap into place
instantly, that delay just leaves the user watching the new asset sit
half-visible until the scrollTo fires, which makes the scroll look
like two separate movements (the ScrollView's auto-adjust on content
size change, then the delayed scrollTo).

Dispatch the scroll on the next runloop instead, so the layout pass
for the new asset finishes first and the scroll runs as a single
smooth movement. Also swap the `.transaction` modifier for the
scoped `.animation(nil, value: assets)` so it only suppresses
animations triggered by `assets` changing — the scroll transaction
on the parent ScrollView is left alone.

* Add animation for both RTL and LTR but on RTL insert assets on the right

* Scroll to head/tail anchor on RTL/LTR attachment insertion

Add invisible zero-sized head and tail anchors bracketing the asset row
so the post-insertion scroll always lands cleanly on the viewport's
right edge. LTR scrolls to the tail anchor, RTL scrolls to the head
anchor (which RTL HStack lays out at the visual right).

Document the broader RTL strategy: assets are reversed so the newest
stays on the visual right in both directions, avoiding HStack's natural
RTL mirroring which forces every existing thumbnail to slide sideways
on each insertion.

ChannelItemDeletedPreviewView, ChannelItemAuthorPreviewView,
ChannelItemAttachmentPreviewView, ChatChannelListItemAttachmentIcon,
and the private LabelWithColon helper with ChannelItemPreview and
ChannelItemPreviewView. ChatChannelListItem.swift now only contains
the top-level item view, the title view, the muted icon, and the
muted-layout style.

* Use tokens.iconSizeSm instead of hard 16 value

* Merge author and attachment preview variants

Replace ChannelItemAuthorPreviewView and ChannelItemAttachmentPreviewView
with a single ChannelItemMessagePreviewView that takes a
ChannelItemPreview.MessageContent and conditionally shows the author
prefix and the attachment icon based on which fields are non-nil. The
shape now mirrors the .message(MessageContent) preview case and the
plain-text branch is also covered by the same view (both decorations
nil), so the conditional dispatch in ChannelItemPreviewView.body
collapses to a single call.

* Rename ChatChannelListItemAttachmentIcon to ChannelListItemAttachmentIcon

* Align muted and attachment icon names with ChannelItem prefix

- ChatChannelListItemMutedIcon -> ChannelItemMutedIcon
- ChannelListItemAttachmentIcon -> ChannelItemAttachmentIcon

All public channel item helper views now share the ChannelItem prefix.

* Fix docs typo in ChannelItemMutedLayoutStyle

* Route channel item typing preview through the view factory

The typing variant of ChannelItemPreview now carries the ChatChannel and
is rendered via factory.makeSubtitleTypingIndicatorView, so customer
overrides of the factory method are honored in the channel list.

ChannelItemPreviewView becomes generic over Factory with a single init
where factory: defaults to DefaultViewFactory.shared and preview: is
labelled, matching the convention used by the rest of the SDK.

* Rename showDelivered to shouldShowDelivered on the item view model

* Demote previewMessageLocalState to public on the item view model

* Expose draft text, author name and attachment icon as open

draftMessageText, messagePreviewAuthorName and previewAttachmentIconImage
are useful when customers override the preview value or build a custom
channel item layout, so promote them to open and group them with the
other preview-related properties on ChatChannelListItemViewModel.

* Consolidate channel item preview text into open messagePreviewText

The two private helpers were picking between
MessagePreviewFormatter.format (which prepends an author label) and
formatContent (which omits it) based on whether the view already renders
an author prefix. Fold that conditional into a single open
messagePreviewText so customers can override the preview text in one
place, and document why the branching exists.

* Demote passthrough item view model properties to public

* Make ChatChannelNavigatableListItem inject a custom item

Mirror ChatThreadListNavigatableItem: the wrapper is now generic over the
channel item and destination and takes the channel item view directly,
with the default ChatChannelListItem built by the factory. The previous
factory/channelName initializer is kept as a deprecated forwarding
overload to preserve source compatibility.

* Remove implementation detail from doc

* Make channel item visibility properties public and drop should prefix

Demote preview, showDelivered, showReadEvents, showMutedTrailingIcon and
showInlineMutedIcon from open to public, and rename the boolean visibility
properties to start with "show" so they read as presentation logic rather
than configuration flags.

* Make thread list item passthrough properties public

* Fix breaking change in navigatible list item

* Move display name to title row section

* Restructure channel item preview into per-variant content types

Replace the preview Kind enum with optional per-variant content values on
ChannelItemPreview, so each variant carries its own value type and the
rendering view selects via if-let rather than a switch.

* Nest channel preview content types under ChannelItemPreview

Expose a nested ChannelItemPreview.Content protocol with per-variant
content types (MessageContent, TypingContent, etc.) so custom variants
can be matched by type. Drop the unused convenience accessors.

* Make ChannelItemPreview and its content protocol Sendable

Refine ChannelItemPreview.Content to Sendable so a preview value can
safely cross actor boundaries under strict concurrency.

* Keep navigatable list item convenience initializers available

Remove the deprecation from the factory-based ChatChannelNavigatableListItem
initializers so existing call sites keep working without warnings.

stripping the animation transaction for all property changes, causing
the timestamp to jump instantly while the rest of the message animated
with the swipe-to-reply spring curve. Scoping it to

content changes while allowing positional animations to propagate.

Fix Xcode 16.1 build (#1430)

* Force @MainActor on MediaLoader completion closures

Swift 6.1 (Xcode 16.4) doesn't always infer that a trailing closure
passed to an `@escaping @MainActor (...) -> Void` parameter is itself
`@MainActor`-isolated, especially when the call site is nested inside
SwiftUI view-builder / `.onAppear` / `.task` closures. Swift 6.2
(Xcode 26.x) relaxed this via improved closure isolation inference, so
the same code compiles there but fails the Xcode 16.x builds
(`Build Demo App (16.4)` and `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)`).

Add explicit `@MainActor` to the trailing closures passed to the new
`MediaLoader` API, `MediaAttachment.generateThumbnail`, and
`MessageController.downloadAttachment` so isolation is unambiguous on
every supported Swift version.

* [CI] Disable xcbeautify/xcpretty in test_ui and build_demo lanes

The previous commit's @MainActor fix still leaves the Xcode 16.4
`Build Demo App (16.4)` and Xcode 16.1 `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)` jobs
red, and we can't see the actual Swift compiler diagnostic because
fastlane scan's formatter (xcbeautify / xcpretty) is swallowing the
`error:` lines emitted by xcodebuild.

Pass `output_style: 'raw'`, `disable_xcpretty: true`, and an empty
`xcodebuild_formatter` to both scan invocations so the raw xcodebuild
output — including the Swift error — makes it into the GH Actions log.

* Work around Swift 6.0 SILGen crash on Utils() default argument

Raw Xcode 16.1 logs show the Swift compiler crashes in SILGen while
synthesizing the default-argument thunk for `utils: Utils = Utils()` on
`StreamChat.init`. The stack trace bottoms out at `emitRawApply` from
`SILGen default arg initializer` at StreamChat.swift:18 (`"Utils("`),
an assertion that was silently fixed in Swift 6.2.

The crash is triggered by `Utils.init` now accepting `mediaLoader:
MediaLoader? = nil` — a protocol-existential parameter from an external
module — combined with `@MainActor` isolation on `Utils` and the fact
that the `Utils()` expression itself lives in another default-argument
slot of a different `@MainActor` initializer.

Move the `Utils()` construction out of the default-argument slot and
into the initializer body by switching `utils` to an optional with a
`nil` default. This is source-compatible: every existing caller of
`StreamChat(chatClient:)`, `StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:)`, and
`StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:utils:)` still type-checks without
changes (`Utils` coerces to `Utils?`).

Fix swipe-to-reply gesture conflicting with message list scrolling (#1431)

* Fix swipe-to-reply gesture blocking message list scrolling

The swipe-to-reply drag recognizer was attached with `.gesture()` and
only compared total translation magnitude against `minimumSwipeDistance`,
with no axis awareness. This caused it to sporadically win the gesture
competition against the enclosing `ScrollView`'s pan recognizer on
diagonal or slow vertical drags, freezing the list until the finger
lifted.

Switch to `.simultaneousGesture(DragGesture())` and gate `offsetX`
updates on a per-event horizontal-dominance check
(`abs(dx) > abs(dy) * 1.5`). The scroll view's pan recognizer always
runs alongside uncontested, and the bubble only moves when the motion
is clearly horizontal. Direction is re-evaluated on every event so no
persistent state can leak across gestures.

* Simplify fix

* Prevent swipe-to-reply from competing with list scrolling

Track the message list scroll phase on newer SwiftUI versions and disable the swipe-to-reply modifier while scrolling is active. This keeps vertical list scrolling in control once a real scroll begins, instead of letting row-level swipe gestures stay attached and interfere.

* Fix edit confirmation briefly flashing send button before microphone

Align the edited/quoted message binding resets with `clearText()`'s

* Fix shared AVPlayer breaking when sending while voice preview plays

Release the shared audio player's reference to the composer's local
voice recording file before the flow can move it into upload. Previously
`confirmRecording`, `discardRecording`, and `sendMessage` left the
singleton AVPlayer playing the local temp URL. On successful upload,
`AttachmentQueueUploader` removes that file, leaving the AVPlayer's
currentItem pointed at a dangling asset and breaking playback for every
voice message in the message list until the player is re-created.

`stopPreviewPlaybackIfNeeded()` only stops the player when the composer
actually has local voice recordings pending/added, so unrelated
message-list playback isn't disrupted on text-only sends.

Fix image attachment flicker on reaction and Giphy not refreshing on shuffle (#1439)

* Fix image attachment loading flicker when reacting to messages

`StreamAsyncImage` previously dropped back to the `.loading` phase
whenever the URL changed — including the trivial change reactions cause
when SwiftUI re-asks for the same attachment with a freshly signed
CDN URL — which produced a brief loading indicator over an
already-cached image.

The view now keeps the previously loaded image on screen until the
loader returns the new one, and only ever surfaces `.loading` when no
image has been rendered yet. The whole `NukeImageLoader` synchronous
cache lookup machinery is gone; `StreamAsyncImage` relies on the
configured `MediaLoader` for caching, which is what every other
loading entry point in the SDK already does.

Resize dimensions are still rounded to integer points so sub-point
layout jitter (for example 251.999 vs 252.0) keeps mapping to the same
CDN URL and the same cache entry.

* Allow seeding StreamAsyncImage with a pre-loaded UIImage

Adds an `image:` parameter to the URL initializer and a UIImage-only
initializer so callers that already have the bitmap in memory can hand
it to `StreamAsyncImage` directly. The seeded image is stored as the
initial `@State` phase, so the very first render shows it — no
placeholder, no loading spinner — and any URL-driven load runs in the
background and replaces the seed once it resolves.

A failed reload no longer wipes a previously rendered image either:
once the view has shown a successful result it stays on screen until a
new successful load arrives, or the view is torn down.

Useful for entry points like the reactions overlay where the message
re-mounts in a fresh view tree and would otherwise start at the empty
phase even when the image is still in the cache.

* Strip query parameters from StreamAsyncImage taskIdentity

even though the image and its size were unchanged.

caching identity for the image is owned by
`StreamCDNRequester.buildCachingKey` at the LLC layer; the SwiftUI
view only needs a stable identifier per `(image path, render size)`
pair so the task doesn't churn.

reactions overlay. On iOS 17 SwiftUI still arbitrates touches through
the recognizer even when `including: .none` is set, which starved
descendant tap recognizers (image attachments, quoted messages, link
previews, …) of touches and made them feel completely unresponsive.

overlay already prevents the inner content from reacting to taps via
`.allowsHitTesting(!shownAsPreview)`, so removing the modifier across
all iOS versions fixes the iOS 17 regression without any visible
behavior change on iOS 18+.

Improve composer RTL support (#1478)

* Fix composer input alignment so spaces render in RTL (IOS-1666)

Forcing `.right`/`.left` text alignment on the composer's UITextView caused
trailing whitespace to be visually trimmed, which made pressing the
spacebar appear to do nothing in an RTL composer. Use `.natural` for the
text view itself so bidi resolves trailing characters correctly, and keep
the explicit alignment on the placeholder label so it still appears on the
expected side of an empty composer.

* Support RTL voice recording gestures and slide-to-cancel (IOS-1668)

The voice recording flow was designed assuming the mic button lives on
the trailing/right edge of the composer and that the user cancels by
swiping left. In RTL the mic sits on the left, so the user naturally
swipes right to cancel, which made the gesture, the slide-to-cancel
label offset, and the cancel threshold all read the wrong values.

Normalize the drag translation in the gesture overlay so downstream
cancel logic always treats negative X as "toward cancel" regardless of
layout direction, and mirror the slide-to-cancel label's visible offset
back into screen coordinates so it follows the finger in both LTR and
RTL.

* Stop attachments tray from shifting on insert in RTL (IOS-1669)

The attachments tray was applying `.animation(.default)` to the whole
container, which animates every implicit layout change as items are
added or removed. In RTL the HStack grows toward the visual leading
edge, so existing attachments appeared to slide whenever a new one
was inserted. Scope the animation to the empty/non-empty transition
so the scale transition still plays once, while individual insertions
no longer drag the rest of the tray around.

Also flip the horizontal offset on the dismiss button overlay so the
close button pokes out of the correct corner in RTL instead of being
nudged back inside the attachment.

* Slide RTL voice cancel label toward duration, not mic (IOS-1668)

`SlideToCancelLabel.slideOffset` was mirroring the X value for RTL, but
SwiftUI's `.offset(x:)` already mirrors its horizontal value in an RTL
layout. Combined, the label slid leftward toward the mic when the user
dragged to cancel in RTL instead of rightward toward the duration.

Drop the explicit RTL mirror on the label offset. The gesture overlay
still normalizes the drag translation so cancel-threshold checks keep
working in both layout directions.

* Anchor RTL attachments tray so existing items stay put (IOS-1669)

Scoping the implicit `.animation(.default)` to `composerAssets.isEmpty`
in the previous attempt only suppressed the entrance/exit animation
from replaying on every insert. The visible shift remained because the
horizontal ScrollView anchors its content to absolute x=0 while an RTL
HStack grows toward the visible leading edge — so appending a new asset
keeps inserting it at x=0 and pushes every already-visible thumbnail to
the right.

Render the assets in reverse order in RTL so newly appended items land
at the off-screen trailing side of the HStack, leaving the existing
thumbnails fixed in place when a new one is added.

* Prepend new RTL attachments instead of reversing the displayed list

Move the RTL fix from a reversed copy computed on every render to a
local @State array that mirrors `assets` in LTR and prepends newly
added entries at index 0 in RTL. The shift was caused by where the
new asset is inserted into the HStack, so the change now happens at
insertion time rather than reordering the entire list on each layout
pass.

* Scroll to the newest attachment after insertion in RTL composer

In LTR the tray scrolls to a tail anchor at the end of the HStack to
reveal the just-inserted asset. In RTL the new asset is prepended and
sits at the visual leading edge (right), so the tail anchor scrolls
the wrong way and the new attachment stays hidden. Scroll to the new
asset's id with the leading anchor in RTL so it's brought back into
view, matching the LTR behavior.

* Let the HStack lay out RTL attachments naturally and scroll to the new one

The previous attempts (reverse the displayed array, then maintain a
local @State and prepend new entries) put the just-added asset at the
visual right in RTL, which doesn't match how the rest of the SDK lays
out trailing content. Drop the custom ordering and rely on HStack's
native RTL behavior so new attachments land at the visual left, then
pick the scroll anchor that matches the current direction (.trailing
in LTR, .leading in RTL) so `scrollTo(tailId, anchor:)` reveals the
new asset on whichever edge it actually landed.

* Snap composer attachment thumbnails on insert and remove

The default layout-shift animation on the HStack made the remaining
thumbnails appear to slide sideways every time an asset was added or
removed. Drop the animation inside the HStack with a transaction so
the thumbnails snap to their new positions. The scroll-to-new-asset
animation lives on the parent ScrollView so it keeps its smooth
behavior.

* Scroll to the new attachment in one smooth movement

The 250ms delay before scrolling existed so the previous layout
animation could settle. Now that the thumbnails snap into place
instantly, that delay just leaves the user watching the new asset sit
half-visible until the scrollTo fires, which makes the scroll look
like two separate movements (the ScrollView's auto-adjust on content
size change, then the delayed scrollTo).

Dispatch the scroll on the next runloop instead, so the layout pass
for the new asset finishes first and the scroll runs as a single
smooth movement. Also swap the `.transaction` modifier for the
scoped `.animation(nil, value: assets)` so it only suppresses
animations triggered by `assets` changing — the scroll transaction
on the parent ScrollView is left alone.

* Add animation for both RTL and LTR but on RTL insert assets on the right

* Scroll to head/tail anchor on RTL/LTR attachment insertion

Add invisible zero-sized head and tail anchors bracketing the asset row
so the post-insertion scroll always lands cleanly on the viewport's
right edge. LTR scrolls to the tail anchor, RTL scrolls to the head
anchor (which RTL HStack lays out at the visual right).

Document the broader RTL strategy: assets are reversed so the newest
stays on the visual right in both directions, avoiding HStack's natural
RTL mirroring which forces every existing thumbnail to slide sideways
on each insertion.

Fix deadlock when building message actions in reactions overlay (#1507)

* Fix reactions overlay layout loop that hangs CI on iOS 26.2

The overlay content height is measured after it is clamped and it also
flips usesScrollView at the same boundary, so a message whose content
sits on that boundary can oscillate by sub-point amounts and never
converge. Ignore sub-point height changes to break the loop.

* Update changelog for reactions overlay layout loop fix

* Apply suggestion from @nuno-vieira

* Fix reactions overlay scroll threshold oscillation on iOS 26.2

The previous 1pt tolerance did not stop the hang because enabling the
scroll view shrinks the measured height by hundreds of points, which
disabled scroll again and re-expanded the content indefinitely.

Track the maximum observed content height separately and derive both the
scroll-view decision and the clamped layout height from that value so
the threshold cannot flip back once scroll is needed.

* Fix deadlock when resolving block actions during overlay layout

Building default message actions called dataStore.currentUser(), which
performs a synchronous Core Data readAndWait during SwiftUI layout and
deadlocks on the managed object context queue. Use the in-memory
currentUserController().currentUser property instead, matching the
existing mute/unmute check in the same method.

* Revert reactions overlay layout changes from this PR

The CI hang is caused by a Core Data deadlock in default message
actions, not a SwiftUI layout loop. Keep this PR scoped to the deadlock
fix only.

Improve Dynamic Type support across the chat UI (#1512)

* Fix quoted reply bubble clipping at large text sizes

The quoted reply bubble used a fixed height that clipped its content at
larger Dynamic Type sizes, leaving the quote indicator short of the text
and collapsing the internal padding. It now grows to fit the quoted
content while keeping a baseline minimum height.

* Fix attachment picker empty-state text truncating at large text sizes

The empty-state guidance in the attachment picker truncated on a single
line at larger Dynamic Type sizes because of a rigid text width. The
text now wraps within a capped width so the guidance stays fully
readable and is never clipped or ellipsized.

The picker panel itself has a fixed height driven by the keyboard
height and never grows with Dynamic Type, so accessibility text sizes
could still make the prompt overflow the panel and overlap the
composer above it. The content is now wrapped in a ScrollView so it
keeps its full, correct Dynamic Type size at every tier, staying
vertically centered when it fits and only becoming interactively
scrollable once it actually overflows the panel (iOS 16.4+).

* Fix commands picker name and format text truncating at large text sizes

Command names were clipped to a fixed 80pt column and format hints
were limited to a single line, so both became unreadable fragments
(e.g. "Gi…", "/mute [@us…") at larger Dynamic Type sizes.

The name column now grows to fit instead of clipping. At accessibility
sizes, the format hint moves below the name onto its own full-width
line and wraps instead of truncating, since there is no longer room
for both on one line.

The row container also lacked a leading alignment, so each row (now
sized to its own content instead of always spanning full width) ended
up centered with an inconsistent left inset per row instead of lining
up with the header above.

Finally, the picker is now only interactively scrollable once its
content actually overflows the available height (iOS 16.4+), instead
of always allowing a scroll/bounce gesture even when everything
already fits on screen.

* Fix no spacing between message rows and replies divider at large text

The "N replies" divider between a thread's parent message and its
replies (and the "new messages" divider) is positioned with a fixed
50pt space reserved above the row, with the divider's own height
capped to match. That fixed size didn't scale with Dynamic Type, so at
larger text sizes the divider's footnote text needed more than 50pt to
render on its own, and the frame cap clipped it, collapsing the
padding and hairlines that normally separate it from the surrounding
messages.

The reservation now grows via a `ScaledMetric` tied to the same
`.footnote` text style used by the divider, so it always has enough
room and keeps proportional spacing from adjacent messages at every
text size. It never shrinks below the configured `newMessagesSeparatorSize`.

* Fix reactions bar plus icon scaling while other icons don't

The "more reactions" plus button used the default SF Symbol rendering,
which follows Dynamic Type and grows with the text size, while the
emoji reaction icons next to it are fixed-size raster assets that
don't scale. At larger text sizes this made the plus icon balloon far
past its circular button and look inconsistent with the rest of the
bar.

The icon is now pinned to a fixed point size, like the other reaction
icons, so every icon in the bar has the same fixed visual weight
regardless of the user's text size setting.

* Keep reactions overlay actions and message within screen bounds

At large Dynamic Type sizes the message actions menu could grow wider
than the screen and spill past its edge. Measure the menu's natural
width and, only when it would overflow, constrain it to the available
width so the row titles truncate instead of running off screen. The
common case keeps its original, unchanged sizing.

* Improve message action items at large text sizes

Action rows previously clipped their titles to a fixed height and always
showed a leading icon, so at large Dynamic Type sizes the labels were cut
off. Rows now grow to fit their title (up to two lines) and drop the icon
at accessibility sizes, matching the system context menu. The reactions
overlay also scrolls as a whole when its content is taller than the
screen, instead of collapsing into an overlapping, unreadable stack.

* Scroll reactions overlay under the top and left-align action titles

Let the whole overlay scroll under the status bar and home indicator when
its content exceeds the screen, matching the UIKit message actions popup.
Action titles now stay leading-aligned (instead of centering) when their
icons are hidden at accessibility text sizes.

* Prevent overlay message preview from overflowing the reactions picker

Let the message preview take its natural height instead of capping it to
the captured frame. Capping made content taller than the frame either bleed
over the reactions picker or, once clipped, drop the timestamp and avatar.
Any genuine overflow is now absorbed by the overlay's scroll. Regenerate
the reactions overlay snapshots.

* Keep annotation button title leading-aligned when it wraps

At accessibility text sizes the "Show Original" action wrapped to a second
line and centered its text. It now stays leading-aligned, matching the
"Translated" label.

* Scale channel list icons with Dynamic Type

The read indicator, muted icon and message preview attachment/deleted/
failed-to-send glyphs now grow together with the surrounding text when the
user increases the Dynamic Type size.

Fix Xcode 16.1 build (#1430)

* Force @MainActor on MediaLoader completion closures

Swift 6.1 (Xcode 16.4) doesn't always infer that a trailing closure
passed to an `@escaping @MainActor (...) -> Void` parameter is itself
`@MainActor`-isolated, especially when the call site is nested inside
SwiftUI view-builder / `.onAppear` / `.task` closures. Swift 6.2
(Xcode 26.x) relaxed this via improved closure isolation inference, so
the same code compiles there but fails the Xcode 16.x builds
(`Build Demo App (16.4)` and `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)`).

Add explicit `@MainActor` to the trailing closures passed to the new
`MediaLoader` API, `MediaAttachment.generateThumbnail`, and
`MessageController.downloadAttachment` so isolation is unambiguous on
every supported Swift version.

* [CI] Disable xcbeautify/xcpretty in test_ui and build_demo lanes

The previous commit's @MainActor fix still leaves the Xcode 16.4
`Build Demo App (16.4)` and Xcode 16.1 `Build SDKs (Old Xcode)` jobs
red, and we can't see the actual Swift compiler diagnostic because
fastlane scan's formatter (xcbeautify / xcpretty) is swallowing the
`error:` lines emitted by xcodebuild.

Pass `output_style: 'raw'`, `disable_xcpretty: true`, and an empty
`xcodebuild_formatter` to both scan invocations so the raw xcodebuild
output — including the Swift error — makes it into the GH Actions log.

* Work around Swift 6.0 SILGen crash on Utils() default argument

Raw Xcode 16.1 logs show the Swift compiler crashes in SILGen while
synthesizing the default-argument thunk for `utils: Utils = Utils()` on
`StreamChat.init`. The stack trace bottoms out at `emitRawApply` from
`SILGen default arg initializer` at StreamChat.swift:18 (`"Utils("`),
an assertion that was silently fixed in Swift 6.2.

The crash is triggered by `Utils.init` now accepting `mediaLoader:
MediaLoader? = nil` — a protocol-existential parameter from an external
module — combined with `@MainActor` isolation on `Utils` and the fact
that the `Utils()` expression itself lives in another default-argument
slot of a different `@MainActor` initializer.

Move the `Utils()` construction out of the default-argument slot and
into the initializer body by switching `utils` to an optional with a
`nil` default. This is source-compatible: every existing caller of
`StreamChat(chatClient:)`, `StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:)`, and
`StreamChat(chatClient:appearance:utils:)` still type-checks without
changes (`Utils` coerces to `Utils?`).

Fix swipe-to-reply gesture conflicting with message list scrolling (#1431)

* Fix swipe-to-reply gesture blocking message list scrolling

The swipe-to-reply drag recognizer was attached with `.gesture()` and
only compared total translation magnitude against `minimumSwipeDistance`,
with no axis awareness. This caused it to sporadically win the gesture
competition against the enclosing `ScrollView`'s pan recognizer on
diagonal or slow vertical drags, freezing the list until the finger
lifted.

Switch to `.simultaneousGesture(DragGesture())` and gate `offsetX`
updates on a per-event horizontal-dominance check
(`abs(dx) > abs(dy) * 1.5`). The scroll view's pan recognizer always
runs alongside uncontested, and the bubble only moves when the motion
is clearly horizontal. Direction is re-evaluated on every event so no
persistent state can leak across gestures.

Fix image attachment flicker on reaction and Giphy not refreshing on shuffle (#1439)

* Fix image attachment loading flicker when reacting to messages

`StreamAsyncImage` previously dropped back to the `.loading` phase
whenever the URL changed — including the trivial change reactions cause
when SwiftUI re-asks for the same attachment with a freshly signed
CDN URL — which produced a brief loading indicator over an
already-cached image.

The view now keeps the previously loaded image on screen until the
loader returns the new one, and only ever surfaces `.loading` when no
image has been rendered yet. The whole `NukeImageLoader` synchronous
cache lookup machinery is gone; `StreamAsyncImage` relies on the
configured `MediaLoader` for caching, which is what every other
loading entry point in the SDK already does.

Resize dimensions are still rounded to integer points so sub-point
layout jitter (for example 251.999 vs 252.0) keeps mapping to the same
CDN URL and the same cache entry.

* Allow seeding StreamAsyncImage with a pre-loaded UIImage

Adds an `image:` parameter to the URL initializer and a UIImage-only
initializer so callers that already have the bitmap in memory can hand
it to `StreamAsyncImage` directly. The seeded image is stored as the
initial `@State` phase, so the very first render shows it — no
placeholder, no loading spinner — and any URL-driven load runs in the
background and replaces the seed once it resolves.

A failed reload no longer wipes a previously rendered image either:
once the view has shown a successful result it stays on screen until a
new successful load arrives, or the view is torn down.

Useful for entry points like the reactions overlay where the message
re-mounts in a fresh view tree and would otherwise start at the empty
phase even when the image is still in the cache.

Improve composer RTL support (#1478)

* Fix composer input alignment so spaces render in RTL (IOS-1666)

Forcing `.right`/`.left` text alignment on the composer's UITextView caused
trailing whitespace to be visually trimmed, which made pressing the
spacebar appear to do nothing in an RTL composer. Use `.natural` for the
text view itself so bidi resolves trailing characters correctly, and keep
the explicit alignment on the placeholder label so it still appears on the
expected side of an empty composer.

* Support RTL voice recording gestures and slide-to-cancel (IOS-1668)

The voice recording flow was designed assuming the mic button lives on
the trailing/right edge of the composer and that the user cancels by
swiping left. In RTL the mic sits on the left, so the user naturally
swipes right to cancel, which made the gesture, the slide-to-cancel
label offset, and the cancel threshold all read the wrong values.

Normalize the drag translation in the gesture overlay so downstream
cancel logic always treats negative X as "toward cancel" regardless of
layout direction, and mirror the slide-to-cancel label's visible offset
back into screen coordinates so it follows the finger in both LTR and
RTL.

* Stop attachments tray from shifting on insert in RTL (IOS-1669)

The attachments tray was applying `.animation(.default)` to the whole
container, which animates every implicit layout change as items are
added or removed. In RTL the HStack grows toward the visual leading
edge, so existing attachments appeared to slide whenever a new one
was inserted. Scope the animation to the empty/non-empty transition
so the scale transition still plays once, while individual insertions
no longer drag the rest of the tray around.

Also flip the horizontal offset on the dismiss button overlay so the
close button pokes out of the correct corner in RTL instead of being
nudged back inside the attachment.

* Slide RTL voice cancel label toward duration, not mic (IOS-1668)

`SlideToCancelLabel.slideOffset` was mirroring the X value for RTL, but
SwiftUI's `.offset(x:)` already mirrors its horizontal value in an RTL
layout. Combined, the label slid leftward toward the mic when the user
dragged to cancel in RTL instead of rightward toward the duration.

Drop the explicit RTL mirror on the label offset. The gesture overlay
still normalizes the drag translation so cancel-threshold checks keep
working in both layout directions.

* Anchor RTL attachments tray so existing items stay put (IOS-1669)

Scoping the implicit `.animation(.default)` to `composerAssets.isEmpty`
in the previous attempt only suppressed the entrance/exit animation
from replaying on every insert. The visible shift remained because the
horizontal ScrollView anchors its content to absolute x=0 while an RTL
HStack grows toward the visible leading edge — so appending a new asset
keeps inserting it at x=0 and pushes every already-visible thumbnail to
the right.

Render the assets in reverse order in RTL so newly appended items land
at the off-screen trailing side of the HStack, leaving the existing
thumbnails fixed in place when a new one is added.

* Prepend new RTL attachments instead of reversing the displayed list

Move the RTL fix from a reversed copy computed on every render to a
local @State array that mirrors `assets` in LTR and prepends newly
added entries at index 0 in RTL. The shift was caused by where the
new asset is inserted into the HStack, so the change now happens at
insertion time rather than reordering the entire list on each layout
pass.

* Scroll to the newest attachment after insertion in RTL composer

In LTR the tray scrolls to a tail anchor at the end of the HStack to
reveal the just-inserted asset. In RTL the new asset is prepended and
sits at the visual leading edge (right), so the tail anchor scrolls
the wrong way and the new attachment stays hidden. Scroll to the new
asset's id with the leading anchor in RTL so it's brought back into
view, matching the LTR behavior.

* Let the HStack lay out RTL attachments naturally and scroll to the new one

The previous attempts (reverse the displayed array, then maintain a
local @State and prepend new entries) put the just-added asset at the
visual right in RTL, which doesn't match how the rest of the SDK lays
out trailing content. Drop the custom ordering and rely on HStack's
native RTL behavior so new attachments land at the visual left, then
pick the scroll anchor that matches the current direction (.trailing
in LTR, .leading in RTL) so `scrollTo(tailId, anchor:)` reveals the
new asset on whichever edge it actually landed.

* Snap composer attachment thumbnails on insert and remove

The default layout-shift animation on the HStack made the remaining
thumbnails appear to slide sideways every time an asset was added or
removed. Drop the animation inside the HStack with a transaction so
the thumbnails snap to their new positions. The scroll-to-new-asset
animation lives on the parent ScrollView so it keeps its smooth
behavior.

* Scroll to the new attachment in one smooth movement

The 250ms delay before scrolling existed so the previous layout
animation could settle. Now that the thumbnails snap into place
instantly, that delay just leaves the user watching the new asset sit
half-visible until the scrollTo fires, which makes the scroll look
like two separate movements (the ScrollView's auto-adjust on content
size change, then the delayed scrollTo).

Dispatch the scroll on the next runloop instead, so the layout pass
for the new asset finishes first and the scroll runs as a single
smooth movement. Also swap the `.transaction` modifier for the
scoped `.animation(nil, value: assets)` so it only suppresses
animations triggered by `assets` changing — the scroll transaction
on the parent ScrollView is left alone.

Improve Dynamic Type support across the chat UI (#1512)

* Fix quoted reply bubble clipping at large text sizes

The quoted reply bubble used a fixed height that clipped its content at
larger Dynamic Type sizes, leaving the quote indicator short of the text
and collapsing the internal padding. It now grows to fit the quoted
content while keeping a baseline minimum height.

* Fix attachment picker empty-state text truncating at large text sizes

The empty-state guidance in the attachment picker truncated on a single
line at larger Dynamic Type sizes because of a rigid text width. The
text now wraps within a capped width so the guidance stays fully
readable and is never clipped or ellipsized.

The picker panel itself has a fixed height driven by the keyboard
height and never grows with Dynamic Type, so accessibility text sizes
could still make the prompt overflow the panel and overlap the
composer above it. The content is now wrapped in a ScrollView so it
keeps its full, correct Dynamic Type size at every tier, staying
vertically centered when it fits and only becoming interactively
scrollable once it actually overflows the panel (iOS 16.4+).

* Fix commands picker name and format text truncating at large text sizes

Command names were clipped to a fixed 80pt column and format hints
were limited to a single line, so both became unreadable fragments
(e.g. "Gi…", "/mute [@us…") at larger Dynamic Type sizes.

The name column now grows to fit instead of clipping. At accessibility
sizes, the format hint moves below the name onto its own full-width
line and wraps instead of truncating, since there is no longer room
for both on one line.

The row container also lacked a leading alignment, so each row (now
sized to its own content instead of always spanning full width) ended
up centered with an inconsistent left inset per row instead of lining
up with the header above.

Finally, the picker is now only interactively scrollable once its
content actually overflows the available height (iOS 16.4+), instead
of always allowing a scroll/bounce gesture even when everything
already fits on screen.

* Fix no spacing between message rows and replies divider at large text

The "N replies" divider between a thread's parent message and its
replies (and the "new messages" divider) is positioned with a fixed
50pt space reserved above the row, with the divider's own height
capped to match. That fixed size didn't scale with Dynamic Type, so at
larger text sizes the divider's footnote text needed more than 50pt to
render on its own, and the frame cap clipped it, collapsing the
padding and hairlines that normally separate it from the surrounding
messages.

The reservation now grows via a `ScaledMetric` tied to the same
`.footnote` text style used by the divider, so it always has enough
room and keeps proportional spacing from adjacent messages at every
text size. It never shrinks below the configured `newMessagesSeparatorSize`.

* Fix reactions bar plus icon scaling while other icons don't

The "more reactions" plus button used the default SF Symbol rendering,
which follows Dynamic Type and grows with the text size, while the
emoji reaction icons next to it are fixed-size raster assets that
don't scale. At larger text sizes this made the plus icon balloon far
past its circular button and look inconsistent with the rest of the
bar.

The icon is now pinned to a fixed point size, like the other reaction
icons, so every icon in the bar has the same fixed visual weight
regardless of the user's text size setting.

* Keep reactions overlay actions and message within screen bounds

At large Dynamic Type sizes the message actions menu could grow wider
than the screen and spill past its edge. Measure the menu's natural
width and, only when it would overflow, constrain it to the available
width so the row titles truncate instead of running off screen. The
common case keeps its original, unchanged sizing.

* Improve message action items at large text sizes

Action rows previously clipped their titles to a fixed height and always
showed a leading icon, so at large Dynamic Type sizes the labels were cut
off. Rows now grow to fit their title (up to two lines) and drop the icon
at accessibility sizes, matching the system context menu. The reactions
overlay also scrolls as a whole when its content is taller than the
screen, instead of collapsing into an overlapping, unreadable stack.

* Scroll reactions overlay under the top and left-align action titles

Let the whole overlay scroll under the status bar and home indicator when
its content exceeds the screen, matching the UIKit message actions popup.
Action titles now stay leading-aligned (instead of centering) when their
icons are hidden at accessibility text sizes.

* Prevent overlay message preview from overflowing the reactions picker

Let the message preview take its natural height instead of capping it to
the captured frame. Capping made content taller than the frame either bleed
over the reactions picker or, once clipped, drop the timestamp and avatar.
Any genuine overflow is now absorbed by the overlay's scroll. Regenerate
the reactions overlay snapshots.

* Keep annotation button title leading-aligned when it wraps

At accessibility text sizes the "Show Original" action wrapped to a second
line and centered its text. It now stays leading-aligned, matching the
"Translated" label.

* Scale channel list icons with Dynamic Type

The read indicator, muted icon and message preview attachment/deleted/
failed-to-send glyphs now grow together with the surrounding text when the
user increases the Dynamic Type size.

Fix channel list rebuilding on every scroll after opening a channel (#1525)

* Fix channel list rebuilding on every scroll after opening a channel

The skippedChannelUpdates flag was set when channel updates were skipped
while a channel was shown, but never reset. After returning to the list,
every row's onAppear then reassigned the whole channels array, forcing a
full list rebuild on each scroll tick. Reset the flag once its queued
update has been applied.

* Avoid copying all channels while iterating the channel list

Iterating with an enumerated array copied every ChatChannel value (a
large struct) on each body evaluation. Iterate the array directly and
resolve a row's index through a lightweight id lookup, which keeps
pagination O(1) without per-row scans or full channel copies.

* Skip re-rendering unchanged channel list items

Make the channel list item and its view model Equatable and apply
.equatable() to the default row, so SwiftUI can skip rebuilding a row's
content when the channel, name, selection and disabled state are
unchanged. The comparison is overridable via isEqual(to:) for subclasses.

* Cache derived values in the channel list item view model

Rendering a row read the preview message, preview/timestamp formatters
and localized strings many times per body evaluation. Compute these once
per instance, which is safe since the view model wraps an immutable
channel snapshot. Subclass overrides bypass the cache as before.

* Skip re-rendering unchanged rows with equatable container

Gate each channel list row behind a ChannelListRowContainer view that
conforms to Equatable and wraps ChatChannel in a reference-counted
ChannelBox so struct copies during the equality check are O(1) instead
of bumping 30+ refcounts. Also reduce local caching limits for members
and watchers in the demo app to lower DTO-to-model conversion cost.

* Remove ChannelBox wrapper now that ChatChannel is a reference type

ChatChannel is now a final class in the LLC, so copies are O(1) by
default. The ChannelBox indirection is no longer needed.
